title: Deep Portrait Quality Assessment. A NTIRE 2024 Challenge Survey
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) Workshops
extended_summary:
This paper is not the requested education study on ChatGPT and academic writing. Instead, it is a computer vision challenge survey for the NTIRE 2024 Portrait Quality Assessment challenge. The paper addresses the problem of automatically estimating the perceptual quality of portrait photographs, especially under difficult real-world conditions such as diverse lighting, blur, motion, framing, and domain shift across scenes and devices. The authors frame portrait quality assessment as a challenging no-reference image quality assessment task where models must rank images by quality and generalize to unseen scenes.

The paper describes the challenge benchmark, datasets, evaluation protocol, baseline models, and the top-performing submitted systems. The challenge relies on the PIQ23 portrait dataset and a private generalization test set. Image quality annotations were created using expert pairwise comparisons and converted into JOD (Just Objectionable Difference) scores through psychometric scaling. The survey then summarizes several model architectures submitted by participating teams, including transformer-based and dual-branch approaches that combine global image features, facial-region analysis, ranking losses, scene adaptation, and pretraining on external image-quality datasets.

No human learners, teachers, or educational institutions were studied. The populations are portrait images and expert annotators used to label image quality, not students. The context is an AI benchmarking/challenge setting in computer vision rather than an educational intervention. Although the paper reports challenge participation numbers and model performance metrics such as SRCC, PLCC, and KRCC, it does not evaluate a classroom technology intervention or any educational outcomes.

The main conclusion is that current deep models still struggle to generalize portrait quality predictions across unseen scenes and higher-quality smartphone domains. Even the best challenge submissions show substantially reduced performance on the hidden challenge test set compared with the public PIQ23 test set, indicating that device/domain shift remains a major obstacle for portrait image quality assessment.
